title: Enclave compliance - STIG residual, audit trail, expiry
description: Generated by scripts/enclave/monitoring.sh. Edit the generator, not this dashboard - Grafana changes live only in its database and are lost with the VM. Fed by the enclave_* textfile facts (monitoring.sh facts) plus node-exporter's systemd collector.

panels.title: Posture - the numbers an assessor asks for first
CAT I open
panels.description: DISA V1R6 severity high, enclave-wide. Anything above zero is the headline.

panels.title: Open (all severities)
panels.description: Total Open V1R6 controls across every reporting machine.

panels.title: Not Reviewed
panels.description: Not Reviewed is not a resting state - each one is an Answer File entry nobody has written yet.

panels.title: Machines in FIPS mode
panels.description: Kernels running with fips_enabled=1. Five is the full enclave.

panels.title: Oldest STIG scan
panels.description: Age of the STALEST checklist. A green board built from a three-week-old scan is not evidence.

panels.title: Reboots pending
panels.description: Machines holding a kernel or library update that is not live until they reboot.

panels.title: STIG residual - is the set stable, and is it shrinking
Open V1R6 controls per machine
panels.description: The acceptance criterion for this enclave is that every machine lands on the SAME residual set. A line that diverges is the interesting result - in either direction.

panels.title: Open by severity, enclave-wide
panels.description: Stacked. high = CAT I.

panels.title: Not Reviewed per machine
panels.description: NR fell 14 -> 9 when five controls were answered from evidence already on the box. A RISING line is usually a check that timed out, not an answer that failed to fire.

panels.title: USG / OpenSCAP failures per machine (V1R1)
panels.description: The other scanner. USG remediates against Canonical's V1R1; Evaluate-STIG only measures, against DISA V1R6. Both numbers are real and they are not the same number.

panels.title: Scan freshness - when did each machine last actually get measured
panels.description: Every number on this dashboard is only as good as these. Sorted stalest first.

panels.title: Audit trail - is it complete, and can it still be written
Audit records LOST
panels.description: auditctl -s lost. Anything above zero means audit records were DROPPED and the trail has holes - a machine can pass every audit rule check while doing this.

panels.title: Audit backlog
panels.description: Backlog approaching the limit is the precursor to lost records.

panels.title: /var/log/audit free space
panels.description: auditd's disk_full_action can HALT the machine, so this partition gets a tighter threshold than any other filesystem: 25%.

panels.title: auditd running
panels.description: 1 = active. From the systemd collector, not from a fact file - this one should never be reported by the machine about itself.

panels.title: AIDE - time since the last check finished
panels.description: dailyaidecheck.timer. Above about 36 hours means the daily check is not running. Absent means AIDE is not installed here at all, which is a different problem.

panels.title: AIDE exit status
panels.description: 0 = clean. Non-zero = AIDE found changes to files it is watching, or failed to run.

panels.title: Failed sudo authentications, 24h rolling
panels.description: pam_faillock here is deny=3 unlock_time=0, so three failures is a PERMANENT lockout until the tally is cleared by hand. This is the early warning.

panels.title: Accounts carrying a faillock tally
panels.description: Users with a non-empty tally in /run/faillock. At 3 they are locked out.

panels.title: sudo invocations, 24h rolling
panels.description: Not a compliance control - an open investigation. MAAS invokes machine-resources via sudo about 1.7 times a SECOND on svc-mgmt-01 (231,159 calls in 38h) and nobody knows why. This panel is here to show whether it is constant or bursty.

panels.title: Patch posture - what is installed, and how current it can possibly be
Machines with security updates pending
panels.description: Updates already available from the mirror these machines can reach - nothing needs carrying in to apply them.

panels.title: Oldest apt metadata
panels.description: THE NUMBER THAT QUALIFIES THE ONE ON ITS LEFT. '0 updates pending' only means 'nothing newer in our mirror snapshot'. If the snapshot is old, that zero says nothing.

panels.title: Third-party packages
panels.description: Installed packages with NO Ubuntu security stream at all - Docker, Harbor components, anything carried in as a .deb. Nobody ships security updates for these into this enclave; each one is accepted risk that should be named.

panels.title: Pro contract remaining
panels.description: When it lapses, FIPS and USG stop receiving updates and the crypto baseline freezes. The replacement token has to be carried in, so this needs lead time.

panels.title: Security updates pending, per machine
panels.description: Security updates are the actionable line. The total includes everything else and is context, not a target - an air-gapped enclave does not chase every package.

panels.title: Age of each machine's package metadata
panels.description: A machine climbing away from the others is pointing at a stale source, not at a stale mirror. All of them climbing together means the mirror needs a transfer.

panels.title: Package inventory by origin
panels.description: Enclave-wide. The bottom two lines are the ones an assessor will ask about: nothing ships security updates for them, so they are accepted risk by definition.

targets.legendFormat: third party - no stream at all

panels.title: Ubuntu Pro services, per machine
panels.description: 1 = enabled. Only in-gap machines publish this. fips-updates and usg must be on inside the boundary; esm-apps being off means the universe packages above are uncovered, which may be a decision but should be a visible one.

panels.title: Expiry - the things that stop working on a date
Certificates, soonest first
panels.description: Time remaining, not a date, so it cannot quietly go stale the way a runbook table does. Orange at 90 days, red at 30.

panels.title: USB storage blocked (V-270718)
panels.description: 1 = usb-storage blocked in modprobe.d, which is the ONLY place the control looks - it never runs lsmod. Drops to 0 for the length of the backup window on host-4, by design.

panels.title: Age of the facts on each machine
panels.description: enclave-facts.timer runs every 15 minutes. If this climbs, every compliance number above it is frozen at whatever it was when the producer last succeeded.

panels.title: Fact sources, per machine
panels.description: 1 = the source was read. 0 = it exists but could not be read. ABSENT ENTIRELY = that source does not exist on that machine, which is NOT the same as zero findings - and telling those two apart is the whole reason this panel exists.
